title: Filters and matching networks
blurb: Tell low-pass from high-pass networks, name filter types by their response, and pick the right filter for a job.

E7C01.why: A low-pass Pi has a **shunt capacitor at input and output with a series inductor between**: the inductor blocks highs, the capacitors shunt them.
E7C01.trap: Two series inductors with a shunt capacitor is a T network, not Pi.

E7C02.why: Series capacitors block low frequencies and a shunt inductor shorts them to ground: **high-pass**.
E7C02.trap: Series L with shunt C would be low-pass; this is the opposite arrangement.

E7C03.why: The extra output inductor adds another filtering element, giving **greater harmonic suppression**.
E7C03.trap: It adds a part, not removes one, and harmonic suppression is the benefit.

E7C04.why: A matching network **cancels the reactive part** and **transforms the resistive part** to the desired value.
E7C04.trap: Reactance is cancelled, never dissipated; it takes no negative resistance.

E7C05.why: **Chebyshev** trades passband ripple for a sharper cutoff than Butterworth.
E7C05.trap: Butterworth has a flat passband, so no ripple.

E7C06.why: **Elliptical** gives the sharpest cutoff and has one or more **notches in the stop band**.
E7C06.trap: An extremely flat passband describes Butterworth, not elliptical.

E7C07.why: A **Pi-L** network is a Pi network with an extra **series inductor at the output**.
E7C07.trap: It has more than three parts: two capacitors and two inductors.

E7C08.why: **Helical** filters are the usual band-pass or notch filters in VHF and UHF transceivers.
E7C08.trap: Sallen-Key and FIR filters are audio or digital filters, not VHF/UHF RF filters.

E7C09.why: A crystal lattice filter uses **quartz crystals** for a sharp, narrow filter on low-level signals.
E7C09.trap: It is a signal filter, not a power-supply filter and not tuned at 1 kHz steps.

E7C10.why: A 2-meter repeater duplexer uses **cavity filters**: sharp and able to handle transmitter power.
E7C10.trap: Crystal filters suit low-level signals, not a duplexer.

E7C11.why: **Shape factor** is the ratio of the 60 dB width to the 6 dB width: a lower value rejects adjacent channels better.
E7C11.trap: Ripple and phase response describe other filter qualities; noise factor is about receiver noise.
